A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SAEmnesia and retain substantial common methods and experiments. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite reorganization and additions.

before.justification: v1 reports original UnlearnCanvas experiments, sequential unlearning, adversarial evaluations, and appendix analyses of model variants and concept interference.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds latent classification experiments, activation visualizations, and nudity-unlearning results on I2P.

M1.justification: The supervised SAE framework remains. v2 generalizes the object/style regularizer to multiple concept groups; Equation (9) also changes squared Pearson correlation to signed correlation, making the documented objective different beyond the OC/DC rename. It adds a two-latent nudity variant within the existing steering framework.

E1.justification: v2 retains UnlearnCanvas object/style coverage and adds nudity removal on I2P, using COCO train 2014 captions for SAE training. This substantially extends the represented data and application beyond the earlier object-erasure evaluation.

E2.justification: The existing UnlearnCanvas and adversarial comparator sets remain. The new nudity comparison in v2 Table 9 substantially expands evaluated comparators, including AdvUn, Receler, MACE, CPE, SLD-M, ESD-x/ESD-u, and unmodified diffusion models.

E3.justification: v2 introduces k-NN evaluation across denoising timesteps and an SD v1.4 nudity protocol using 30K COCO captions, NudeNet threshold 0.6, CLIPScore, and FID. Its one-latent and two-latent nudity settings also use different multipliers, -49 and -60, so their comparison does not isolate latent count.

E4.justification: v2 adds direct tests of whether one latent preserves classification information, spatial activation comparisons for Architectures and Rabbits, and comparisons of one- versus two-latent nudity removal. These substantially extend the earlier score-distribution, interference, loss-variant, and multiplier analyses, which are retained.

E5.justification: Both appendices report the same four-seed means and standard deviations. v2 introduces no additional repeated-run disclosure, confidence intervals, or statistical testing practices.

E6.justification: Existing UnlearnCanvas and adversarial numbers remain unchanged. v2 adds k-NN findings, activation maps, revised qualitative examples, and I2P results: 47 detections for one latent, 9 for TOP2, and 18 for SAeUron. It also corrects the Flowers discussion from 0.015 and 2.67-fold to 0.0166 and 2.43-fold, matching values already plotted in v1.

T1.justification: v2 formalizes multiple disjoint concept groups and changes Equation (9) from averaging squared correlations to averaging signed correlations, which has different mathematical behavior. Batch notation is clarified elsewhere, but no theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The central single-latent, computational-efficiency, UnlearnCanvas, and sequential-unlearning claims remain. v2 adds prominent claims of effective, state-of-the-art nudity suppression on I2P and removes the abstract's assertion that training overhead consists only of cross-entropy computation.

C2.justification: v1's substantive cautions about evaluation scope, architectural transfer, and intervention-point dependence are removed, while v2 asserts architecture-agnostic applicability. v2 adds explanations involving style-entangled flames/jellyfish and imbalanced nudity training data weakening centralization. These substantially revise applicability and failure discussions.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies the nine-object sequence and cumulative steering, qualitative settings of multiplier -1 over the final 25 steps, and nudity prompts and multipliers. These expand reproducibility information without establishing reruns of retained experiments. Existing loss weights remain, while v1's explicit L1 normalization formula is omitted.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting the nudity comparisons and the use of SD v1.x as a standard evaluation setting, while removing the SDXL-Turbo SAE reference and discussion. The central positioning against unsupervised SAE-based unlearning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 extensively rewrites the abstract and conclusion, adds an explicit contribution list, and combines Experiments and Results into structured setup, quantitative, qualitative, and additional-experiment subsections. Method explanations are streamlined, terminology is standardized, and the dedicated limitations structure is removed.

P2.justification: v2 converts paired score plots into overlays and sequential-result tables into plots, adds k-NN and activation-map figures and a nudity table, and revises the pipeline illustration. Figure 1 and appendix qualitative grids contain replacement examples, while several retained tables and figures are relocated.

improvement.justification: The new classification and activation analyses strengthen support for feature centralization, and I2P evaluation broadens evidence while disclosing the one-latent failure. However, v2's Equation (9) can reward anticorrelation instead of decorrelation, and substantive architectural limitations disappear. The PDFs do not resolve whether the changed objective was intended or used; these gains and losses prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
